bodyMarkdown:
## Dentist Salary Melbourne: No Award, but Strong Earnings

If you're searching for "dentist salary Melbourne", you're likely trying to understand what dentists earn in the city and how to convert an hourly rate or salary offer into an annual figure. Unlike many professions, dentists in private practice are not covered by a modern award. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that no award names dentists, so award-free employees are entitled only to the National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) and the National Employment Standards. In practice, however, dentist pay is much higher, as shown by data from the Australian Taxation Office and the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

This guide uses the latest official figures to explain what a dentist salary Melbourne might look like, how to convert between hourly and annual pay, and what tax and super mean for your take-home pay. We'll also cover the fortnightly amounts and the distinction between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and actual market earnings.

## What the Data Says About Dentist Pay

The most authoritative source for dentist earnings is the ATO's taxation statistics. For the 2023–24 income year, 8,859 people who listed their occupation as dentist (code 252312) reported an average taxable income of $162,722 and a median of $131,588. For those who received salary or wages (rather than business income), the average was $108,448 and the median was $95,289. These figures include part-time and full-time workers, so they are not a full-time salary rate.

Jobs and Skills Australia, using ABS data from May 2025, reports median full-time earnings for Dental Practitioners (ANZSCO 2523) at $3,232 per week, or about $168,064 per year. This group includes dental specialists as well as dentists, and covers only employees (not practice owners or contractors). About 60% of dental practitioners work full-time hours, averaging 42 hours per week.

For a dentist salary Melbourne, these national figures are the best available; no separate Melbourne-specific data is published. The ATO data covers all states and territories, and Melbourne's earnings are likely similar to the national median.

## Converting Hourly to Annual: The Formula

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the standard formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a full-time week, we assume 38 hours (the standard used by the Fair Work Ombudsman for the National Minimum Wage).

For example, if you are offered an hourly rate of $66.60 (the approximate hourly equivalent of the median taxable income of $131,588), your annual gross would be:

$66.60 × 38 × 52 = $131,588

If you are paid a salary or wage of $95,289 (the median for employed dentists), the hourly rate would be about $48.22 ($95,289 ÷ 1,976 hours).

You can also work backwards: if you know your annual salary, divide by 52 to get a weekly figure, then divide by your weekly hours to find the hourly rate. The fortnightly amount is simply the weekly figure multiplied by 2. For the median taxable income of $131,588, the fortnightly gross is about $5,061 ($131,588 ÷ 26).

## Tax and Super on a Dentist Salary

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200, then:

- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For the median taxable income of $131,588, the tax would be approximately $29,996 and the Medicare levy $2,632, leaving take-home pay of about $98,960 per year, or $3,806 per fortnight. If you have a HELP debt, an additional compulsory repayment applies (about $9,346 at that income level).

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a dentist earning $131,588, the super contribution would be about $15,791 per year, added to your pay by your employer. This is not deducted from your salary; it's an extra cost for the employer.

## Casual Loading and Other Considerations

If you work as a casual dentist, you may be entitled to a casual loading. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour, which includes a 25% loading on the base rate of $26.44. However, since dentists are award-free, there is no mandated casual loading under a modern award. Your employer may still offer a loading as part of your contract. On [the timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add 25% casual loading on top. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

Remember that the figures in this guide are estimates. Annual pay calculated here assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide). HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

For more detailed pay calculations, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for other occupations or use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool. Always check your specific employment contract and consult a tax professional for personalised advice.
